newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sells remaining holding in estate firm.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sells remaining holding in estate firm.

text.p: The Sri Lanka government on Tuesday sold its remaining shareholding in the previously privatised Agalawatte Plantations Ltd but held back a key token share, an official said.

The official from the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), which oversees privatisations, told Reuters that the government sold 3.8 million shares of Agalawatte Plantations on the Colombo Stock Exchange at 35.50 rupees each.
"With this sale, the government has reduced its holding in Agalawatte to one 'golden share'," said the PERC official.
The golden share enables the government to intervene in the company in the event of malpractices.
"The balance of government holdings in the other listed firms will also be probably sold through the stock exchange," said the official.

The government privatised Kegalle Plantations, Kelani Valley Plantations, Bogawantalawa Plantations,, Agalawatte Plantations, Horana Plantations and Kotagala Plantations in 1995 by selling 51 percent to a strategic investor and 20 percent to the public.
Ten percent was reserved for estate workers while the government retained 19 percent or 3.8 million shares in each firm.
Sri Lanka began restructuring the 23 plantation firms which own some 600,000 hectares of tea, rubber and coconut in 1992 by privatising management, which later spread to ownership.
